full_judgment:
"We make it clear that if the writ petitioners desire to redress their grievances before the Administrative Tribunal since they had been prosecuting their grievances in the Supreme Court of Bangladesh for a long time, the Administrative Tribunal shall entertain their petitions, if any, are filed on condoning the delay under section 14 of the Limitation Act. We also waive the statutory bar applicable to an applicant for filling a depart-mental appeal before the appellate authority, since they have already moved the High Court Division; the said period of limitation has already expired. We want to make it clear that the provision to sub section (4) shall not stand in the way in making the applications and the Administrative Tribunal shall admit the petitions as if the applicants have preferred appeals under proviso to sub section (4)." 

 15. In the result, the Rule is discharged, however, without any order as to cost. But in the context of the above decision of the Appellate Division limitation would not operate as bar if the petitioner, if so advised, files his case before the Administrative Tribunal.
